account_health_score.gap_note: The account health score is a fitted model output (analytics/health_score.py) computed at a single as-of date over the active accounts, not a mart_* column and not held as a monthly history -- querying it needs the scoring model, not a SQL aggregation. Its four inputs are queryable separately where a mart column carries them.
account_health_score.name: Account health score

account_specific_baseline_deviation.gap_note: Restates its parent rather than adding a series: usage-dip breadth, the parent's value, is already the aggregated account-relative baseline deviation, and it is computed in analytics/variance_diagnostic.py, not served from a mart_* table. A separate leaf would repeat it.
account_specific_baseline_deviation.name: Account-specific baseline deviation

activation.formula: Days from provisioning to first production Action
activation.gap_note: Blended TTFA is identically 0 in the current generated data (fact_usage_monthly is monthly grain -- every account's first Action lands in its own signup month). Real, not fabricated, just degenerate on this data.
activation.name: Activation
activation.note: shared driver for new-logo conversion and future expansion

am_cost_by_segment.gap_note: Fully-loaded cost (OTE x loading factor, accrued from hire to departure) of the segment's AM-Commercial / AM-Enterprise reps. A real 0 for SMB, which has no AM.
am_cost_by_segment.name: AM cost by segment (comp, ramp status, book size)

am_efficiency.formula_note: (numerator covered under Growth; AM cost expanded below)
am_efficiency.gap_note: Ratio of summed monthly expansion MRR movement (am_expansion_arr / 12) to summed AM cost, over rows where an AM exists. Commercial and Enterprise only: SMB has no AM, so the ratio is undefined there and a request for SMB is rejected as segment_not_available rather than returned as an empty value. Month grain is seasonal; use grain=year for a stable read.
am_efficiency.name: AM efficiency

query.numerator: case when am_cost > 0 then am_expansion_arr / 12.0 end

am_sentiment_notes.gap_note: Mean AM sentiment score over the account-months that have one. Sentiment exists only where an AM touchpoint was logged: absent for 96% of SMB account-months, 53% of Commercial and 28% of Enterprise, so an SMB cut is nearly empty.
am_sentiment_notes.name: AM sentiment notes

am_touch_effectiveness.gap_note: fact_am_activity exists but no mart exposes AM touches joined to a recommitment outcome; mart_efficiency exposes only the touch count.
am_touch_effectiveness.name: AM touch effectiveness (recommitment conversations)

am_touchpoint_volume.name: AM touchpoint volume (book size, ramp status, check-in cadence)
am_touchpoint_volume.note: book size, ramp status, check-in cadence

automated_action_volume_delivered.name: Automated Action volume delivered (usage growth, account count)

avg_initial_commitment.formula: Realized deal size at close, by segment
avg_initial_commitment.name: Avg initial commitment

brand_awareness.gap_note: No web-traffic, branded-search, or share-of-voice source exists anywhere in this project's raw data.
brand_awareness.name: Brand & awareness

branded_search_volume_trend.gap_note: No web-traffic/search source exists in any layer of this project.

cac_by_channel.gap_note: mart_efficiency exposes blended_cac (already blended across channels by each channel's share of the segment's new accounts) -- the tree's own per-channel 'unblended' cut is not exposed by any mart_* table, so `channel` is listed in allowed_dimensions per the tree but is NOT in queryable_dimensions until a Phase 2 mart change exposes it.
cac_by_channel.name: CAC by channel (unblended)

churn_reason_category.gap_note: Needs a churn reason per churned account, loud (explicit cancellation) versus silent (non-renewal). No churn, subscription or account record carries a reason or mode field; tenure_at_churn is the only churn-event attribute available.
churn_reason_category.name: Churn reason category (loud vs. silent)

cohort_comparison.gap_note: No mart_* table exposes an account-type x usage-cycle cohort baseline.
cohort_comparison.name: Cohort comparison (same account type, same period last cycle)
cohort_comparison.note: same account type, same period last cycle

Company-wide only: no segment cut.
community_events.name: Community/events

consumption_payback.formula_note: — excludes committed-but-unused capacity; flat ~80% gross margin assumed
consumption_payback.name: Consumption payback
consumption_payback.scope_note: by segment (utilized Actions only, not billed)

contraction_churned_consumption_revenue.formula: Driven by account health decline and lost renewals, by segment
contraction_churned_consumption_revenue.name: Contraction + churned consumption revenue

cost_per_channel_activity.gap_note: Cost per channel activity (cost/MQL, cost/SDR meeting) needs channel spend joined to per-channel lead and meeting counts. The cost side exists (mart_efficiency.sm_cost), and fact_leads / fact_sales_activities exist, but no mart_* table joins channel cost to those counts.
cost_per_channel_activity.name: Cost per channel activity (cost/MQL, cost/SDR meeting)

cyclical_planned_usage_dip_vs_structural.formula: Normalized against the account's own historical baseline or cohort
cyclical_planned_usage_dip_vs_structural.gap_note: The tree's full cyclical-vs-structural classification needs a same-account-type/same-period cohort baseline that no mart_* table exposes; only the underlying account-relative usage signal exists (mart_account_health), and it is not pre-aggregated into a queryable ratio.
cyclical_planned_usage_dip_vs_structural.name: Cyclical/planned usage dip vs. structural churn

deal_size_trend_within_segment_band.gap_note: Won-count-weighted share of won new-business deals at or below the segment's ACV band floor. Deal amounts are clipped to the band at generation, so this measures how often the clip binds: 53% of Commercial wins sit at the floor and no Enterprise win does. Variation inside the band is compressed.
deal_size_trend_within_segment_band.name: Deal-size trend within segment band

query.denominator: case when share_won_at_band_floor is not null then new_business_won_count end

declining_share_of_full_chain_vs_partial.gap_note: Share of chain accounts at or above the 0.70 completion threshold: exactly the complement of workflow_chain_under_utilization, so it adds no information beyond it.
declining_share_of_full_chain_vs_partial.name: Declining share of full-chain vs. partial-chain runs

direct_traffic_share.gap_note: No web-traffic source exists in any layer of this project.
direct_traffic_share.name: Direct traffic share

discount_rate_vs_list.gap_note: Amount-weighted discount on won new-business deals (1 - won amount / won list price). List price is generated as amount / (1 - discount rate), so this is an identity up to rounding rather than an independent check on pricing.
discount_rate_vs_list.name: Discount rate vs. list

engagement_login_frequency.gap_note: Mean logins per active account-month (a real 0 where an account had no login).
engagement_login_frequency.name: Engagement / login frequency

existing_account_community_engagement_de.gap_note: The build spec's community_membership source was never generated.
existing_account_community_engagement_de.name: Existing-account community engagement depth

ingestion_without_completion_rate.gap_note: Actions-weighted: 1 - downstream Actions / upstream Actions (a ratio of sums, so it weights accounts by volume).
ingestion_without_completion_rate.name: Ingestion-without-completion rate

lead_recycling_nurture_re_qualification_.gap_note: Needs lead status history (a lead returning to nurture and re-qualifying). fact_leads has one row per lead with no status changes, and fact_lead_scoring_history's re-scores are not a re-qualification event.
lead_recycling_nurture_re_qualification_.name: Lead recycling / nurture re-qualification rate

loss_reason_mix.gap_note: Scalar view of a three-way mix: the competitive share of lost new-business opportunities. The tree names competitive, no-decision and price; the mart carries all four reason counts (competitive, no-decision, price, other) but this node serves the competitive share only.
loss_reason_mix.name: Loss-reason mix (competitive / no-decision / price)

loud_explicit_cancellation_vs_silent_non.gap_note: Needs each churn classified as an explicit cancellation (loud) or a non-renewal (silent). No record carries that classification: subscription status is active, churned, renewed, expanded or contracted with no reason or mode field, and a lost renewal opportunity records a loss_reason (price, no_decision, competitive, other) that is not a cancellation-versus-lapse flag.
loud_explicit_cancellation_vs_silent_non.name: Loud (explicit cancellation) vs. silent (non-renewal) mix

ltv_by_segment_acquisition_channel.formula: Cumulative margin-adjusted revenue over a modeled retention-weighted horizon, by segment × acquisition channel
ltv_by_segment_acquisition_channel.formula_note: — 5-year horizon, flat 10% annual discount rate, same ~80% gross margin assumption as Consumption payback (reused, not re-derived). Built from a retention-curve input (Kaplan-Meier logo survival by entry segment, observed while enough accounts are at risk and extended forward past that point by a constant monthly hazard; compounding GRR is rejected, because monthly GRR counts month-to-month usage contraction, not whether the account is still a customer — `retention_cohorts.py` already tested acquisition channel as a retention driver and found no comparable differentiation, and this node's channel cut is shown for SMB only, where it carries signal through CAC, not through differential retention), an expansion-trajectory input (observed MRR per surviving account by age, which embeds expansion, overage and segment graduation; wallet share progression is not computable, so nothing is modeled from it), and the LTV : CAC ratio against both CAC bases: marketing-only, and rep-loaded (ISR cost for Commercial, AE and SE cost for Enterprise per won logo; AM cost excluded). LTV is by entry segment; Commercial and Enterprise are ranges, Enterprise directional only, and the marketing-only ratio is not decision-grade where reps are the acquisition cost. `mart_efficiency.blended_cac`, and so Consumption payback, stays marketing-only (the same fully-loaded-cost gap that already caveats payback and its `level_comparability: caveated` status); don't present this ratio as more trustworthy than the payback figure it extends.
ltv_by_segment_acquisition_channel.gap_note: A non-additive diagnostic overlay on Consumption payback with no children and no mart-backed series, so query_metric serves no data for it. The modeled lifetime view (survival by entry segment, MRR per surviving account, margin and CAC) is computed outside the mart engine by analytics/ltv_by_segment.py: Commercial and Enterprise as ranges, SMB split by acquisition channel, the channel difference being a CAC difference. Query consumption_payback for the single-window recovery read it extends.
ltv_by_segment_acquisition_channel.name: LTV by segment × acquisition channel
ltv_by_segment_acquisition_channel.note: **non-additive** diagnostic overlay on payback, not a mathematical child — payback is a single-window recovery ratio; LTV extends the same CAC-efficiency question over the account's full modeled life

magic_number.formula: Net new ARR ÷ prior-period S&M cost
magic_number.formula_note: (numerator covered under Growth; S&M cost expanded below)
magic_number.gap_note: Ratio of summed net new ARR to summed PRIOR-period S&M cost, over rows where a prior-period cost exists (first month: 2023-02). At month grain a single month is noisy and can be negative (net new ARR carries the raw data's Q4 seasonality); use grain=year for a stable read. SMB carries no rep cost, so its ratio reflects program spend only and is not comparable to Commercial/Enterprise. S&M cost is the tree's three-part definition (rep fully-loaded cost + marketing spend); marketing-team headcount is not in the raw data, so the ratio is a ceiling.
magic_number.name: Magic number

query.numerator: case when magic_number_sm_cost is not null then net_new_arr end

marketing_sales_handoff_quality.gap_note: No MQL or SAL lifecycle stage exists in the lead funnel: fact_leads carries ids, channel, created_date, converted_date, is_converted, lead_score and days_to_conversion, and the raw leads source has no stage or status field. Leads and campaign touches measure conversion to signup, not the marketing-to-sales handoff.
marketing_sales_handoff_quality.name: Marketing–sales handoff quality
marketing_sales_handoff_quality.note: diagnostic overlay on the above three, not a fourth multiplicative factor

marketing_spend_allocation_by_channel.gap_note: mart_efficiency exposes channel spend summed over channels and attributed to segment (by each segment's share of the channel-month's new accounts) -- the tree's per-channel split is not exposed by any mart_* table, so `channel` is listed in allowed_dimensions per the tree but is NOT in queryable_dimensions.
marketing_spend_allocation_by_channel.name: Marketing spend allocation by channel

mid_chain_workflow_abandonment.gap_note: Share of chain accounts partial in this month and in the calendar-prior month (the playbook rule's two-consecutive-month idea; 0.70 threshold proposed, not confirmed). Subject to the same end-of-window fall-away as the parent node.
mid_chain_workflow_abandonment.name: Mid-chain workflow abandonment

mql_response_sla.gap_note: Needs a per-lead MQL timestamp and the first sales touch on that lead. Neither exists: fact_sales_activities is keyed to opportunity_id with no lead_id, and the only lifecycle timestamp on a lead is the signup (converted_date). days_to_conversion is lead-to-signup time, not time-to-first-sales-touch.
mql_response_sla.name: MQL response SLA (time to first sales touch)

mql_sal_acceptance_rate.gap_note: Needs an MQL and SAL stage, or an accept/reject disposition, per lead. fact_leads records only convert vs. not, which is the lead-to-PQL rate inside Pipeline generated.
mql_sal_acceptance_rate.name: MQL → SAL acceptance rate

new_logo_consumption_revenue.formula: Pipeline generated × win rate × avg initial commitment
new_logo_consumption_revenue.name: New logo consumption revenue

nrr.formula: (Starting − Contraction − Churn + Expansion) ÷ Starting consumption revenue
nrr.name: NRR

onboarding_completion_rate.gap_note: Identically 1.0 in every month of the current generated data -- every account produces a first Action in its signup month (usage is recorded monthly), so the series carries no variance signal. Partial, matching the variance-diagnostic engine.
onboarding_completion_rate.name: Onboarding completion rate

onboarding_cs_efficiency.formula: Manual AM/CS touchpoints ÷ volume of automated Actions delivered
onboarding_cs_efficiency.name: Onboarding/CS efficiency

detail: Organic traffic growth, by source (docs, blog, SEO)

organic_content.gap_note: Computed and validated by analytics/marketing_attribution.py from fact_leads and fact_campaign_engagement_events (the variance-diagnostic engine reads that computation), but it rests on point-in-time lead-resolution logic rather than a SQL aggregation over a mart_* table, and no mart_* rollup of it exists, so query_metric cannot serve it. Company-wide only: no segment cut.
organic_content.name: Organic/content

outbound_sdr_and_segment_graduation_volu.gap_note: Not a separately computed leaf: the tree tracks outbound SDR and segment-graduation volume under win rate and the company model's segment-migration branch rather than duplicating it here. Query win_rate for the closed-deal side; segment graduation is carried by mart_segment_migration, which query_metric does not serve.
outbound_sdr_and_segment_graduation_volu.name: Outbound SDR and segment-graduation volume — tracked under win rate and the company model's migration branch, not duplicated here
outbound_sdr_and_segment_graduation_volu.note: Outbound SDR and segment-graduation volume — tracked under win rate and the company model's migration branch, not duplicated here

overage_realization.formula: Overage billing realized against usage crossing committed minimums
overage_realization.gap_note: Overage MRR as a share of total MRR, in dollars. A realization rate is 100% on every account-month (billed MRR = unit price x the larger of committed and utilized Actions, so all overage usage is billed); the dollar share is the series with variance in it. Commercial and Enterprise only (SMB carries no commitment).
overage_realization.name: Overage realization

paid.gap_note: Computed and validated by analytics/marketing_attribution.py from fact_leads and fact_campaign_engagement_events (the variance-diagnostic engine reads that computation), but it rests on point-in-time lead-resolution logic rather than a SQL aggregation over a mart_* table, and no mart_* rollup of it exists, so query_metric cannot serve it. Company-wide only: no segment cut.
paid.name: Paid

pipeline_generated.formula: Σ over channels (channel volume × channel-to-lead rate × lead-to-PQL rate)
pipeline_generated.gap_note: Computed and validated by analytics/marketing_attribution.py from fact_leads and fact_campaign_engagement_events (the variance-diagnostic engine reads that computation), but it rests on point-in-time lead-resolution logic rather than a SQL aggregation over a mart_* table, and no mart_* rollup of it exists, so query_metric cannot serve it. Company-wide only: no segment cut.
pipeline_generated.name: Pipeline generated

poc_pass_rate.gap_note: Enterprise only, as the tree specifies: passed POCs over closed new-business opportunities (won or lost) with a POC outcome, by close month. Monthly n is small (about 10-15 from 2023, fewer before), so a single month is noisy; read it by quarter or year for a stable figure. A POC can fail on a won deal (22 of 113 Enterprise wins).
poc_pass_rate.name: POC pass rate (Enterprise)
poc_pass_rate.segment_unavailable_reason: has no POC data for segment '{segment}': proof-of-concept outcomes exist only in the Enterprise motion, so the source mart ({source_mart}) has no POC outcomes for any other segment; the metric is defined for {queryable_segments} only.

quickstart_docs_content_engagement_rate.gap_note: The build spec's content_engagement source was never generated -- no mart or fact table carries docs/quickstart interaction at all.
quickstart_docs_content_engagement_rate.name: Quickstart/docs content engagement rate

renewal_win_rate.gap_note: Closed-won renewals over closed renewals (opportunity_type = renewal), by close month. Commercial and Enterprise only (SMB has no renewal opportunities). Renewal opportunities close from 2021-02 for Commercial and from 2022-07 for Enterprise, so earlier months are empty.
renewal_win_rate.name: Renewal win rate

rep_capacity_ramp_mix.gap_note: Share of closed new-business opportunities created within 180 days of the owning rep's hire date. Approximate: the owner is the current rep after any reassignment on a departure, so ramp attribution is not exact. Commercial and Enterprise only (SMB has no rep).
rep_capacity_ramp_mix.name: Rep capacity / ramp mix

rep_fully_loaded_cost_incl_ramp.gap_note: All rep types of the segment (ISR, AE, SE, AM-Commercial, AM-Enterprise), accruing from hire date so ramping reps are included; mart_efficiency.rep_ramp_cost isolates the ramp-window share. A real 0 for SMB.
rep_fully_loaded_cost_incl_ramp.name: Rep fully-loaded cost, incl. ramp

s_m_cost.gap_note: Rep fully-loaded cost + marketing spend allocated to the segment. NULL before 2023-01, when marketing spend begins. Marketing-team headcount is not in the raw data, so this is a floor.
s_m_cost.name: S&M cost

see_growth_contraction_churn_drivers.gap_note: Defined by reference in the tree ('See Growth -- contraction, churn drivers') -- query contraction_churned_consumption_revenue and its children instead.
see_growth_contraction_churn_drivers.name: See Growth — contraction, churn drivers

see_growth_expansion_contraction_churn_d.gap_note: Defined by reference in the tree ('See Growth -- expansion, contraction, churn drivers') -- query nrr_expansion/contraction/churn via expansion_consumption_revenue and contraction_churned_consumption_revenue instead.
see_growth_expansion_contraction_churn_d.name: See Growth — expansion, contraction, churn drivers
see_growth_expansion_contraction_churn_d.note: See Growth — expansion, contraction, churn drivers

see_growth_expansion_revenue_drivers.gap_note: Defined by reference in the tree ('See Growth -- expansion revenue drivers'), not a leaf with its own actual -- query expansion_consumption_revenue and its children instead.
see_growth_expansion_revenue_drivers.name: See Growth — expansion revenue drivers

share_of_voice_vs_named_competitors.gap_note: No competitive-intelligence source exists in any layer of this project.
share_of_voice_vs_named_competitors.name: Share of voice vs. named competitors

stage_to_stage_conversion.gap_note: Degenerate by construction: every new-business deal logs every stage of its segment's path (SAL, SQO, Proposal/Negotiation, plus POC for Enterprise), won or lost, so the share of deals advancing at each hop is 100% in every month and carries no variance signal. Deals differ in how long they spend in each stage (mart_deal_funnel.avg_days_in_*), not in whether they reach it.
stage_to_stage_conversion.name: Stage-to-stage conversion (SAL → SQO → POC → Proposal → Close)

support_ticket_volume_severity.gap_note: Severity-weighted ticket load per active account-month: ticket count times average severity (low=1 to critical=4), summed, over the number of account-months. One scalar for two attributes; the mart carries volume and severity separately.
support_ticket_volume_severity.name: Support ticket volume / severity

tenure_at_churn.gap_note: Computed as avg(account_tenure_days) filtered to rows where month = churn_month -- the mean tenure, in days, of accounts that churned within the requested window.
tenure_at_churn.name: Tenure-at-churn (early vs. late lifecycle)

time_to_first_integration_first_successf.gap_note: No integration or first-successful-run event exists in the raw data; fact_usage_monthly is monthly grain with no first-Action timestamp.
time_to_first_integration_first_successf.name: Time-to-first-integration / first successful run

time_to_respond_on_churn_risk_flag.gap_note: Needs a churn-risk flag event joined to AM response; no mart_* table exposes it.
time_to_respond_on_churn_risk_flag.name: Time-to-respond on churn-risk flag

usage_trend.gap_note: The account-relative usage signal (the share of active accounts whose trailing 3-month mean Actions sits below 70% of their own cumulative mean) is computed by analytics/variance_diagnostic.py from mart_account_health's actions_consumed, not a plain mart column, so query_metric cannot serve it as a SQL aggregation.
usage_trend.name: Usage trend (account-relative baseline)

utilized_vs_committed_action_volume.gap_note: mart_efficiency exposes the resulting utilization-haircut margin, not the raw utilized/committed ratio the tree names -- movement here can come from either utilization or the underlying MRR base.
utilized_vs_committed_action_volume.name: Utilized vs. committed Action volume

wallet_share_progression.formula: % of an account's total addressable workflow footprint running through Acme Corp
wallet_share_progression.gap_note: Requires an account's total addressable workflow footprint (the ratio's denominator) -- no source in this project estimates an account's non-Acme workflow volume.
wallet_share_progression.name: Wallet share progression

win_rate.gap_note: SMB always shows win_rate = 1.0 (every SMB opportunity is created already Closed Won -- build spec Section 2); the tree itself notes SMB 'has no win-rate concept to true up', so a Commercial/Enterprise segment filter is the meaningful read.
win_rate.name: Win rate

workflow_chain_under_utilization.formula: Upstream/trigger Actions occur but downstream/completion Actions sit idle
workflow_chain_under_utilization.gap_note: Share of accounts with a workflow chain whose full-chain completion rate is below the 0.70 threshold (the playbook rule's value, proposed and not confirmed). Partial chains exist only in the 5 months before a churn, and churns after the end of the data window are not observed, so the series falls away across the last 5 months of the window (partial-chain accounts fall from about 300 a month in mid-2025 to 4 in 2025-12); the variance engine blanks those 5 months, this query does not.
workflow_chain_under_utilization.name: Workflow chain under-utilization

workflow_migration_rate.gap_note: Needs business-process-level onboarding events; not generated.
workflow_migration_rate.name: Workflow migration rate (new business processes onboarded per quarter)
workflow_migration_rate.note: new business processes onboarded per quarter
